payload.body: Spectral-band-spread is a spectral analysis parameter quantifying the dispersion of spectral energy across the frequency bins within a defined frequency sub-band of a spectrum at a given analysis frame. It is the square root of the band's second central moment: the energy-weighted standard deviation of bin frequencies about the band's centroid. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds (f_low, f_high), (2) the per-bin energy values E_i = |X[k]|^2 for bins whose center frequencies fall within [f_low, f_high), (3) the analysis frame window. Computed as spread = sqrt( sum E_i * (f_i - c)^2 / sum E_i ), where c = sum(f_i * E_i) / sum(E_i) is the spectral-band-centroid of the same band. The value is in hertz: a large spread means energy is dispersed across the band, a small spread means energy is concentrated near the centroid. Persistence: the standardized mathematical definition of band dispersion in spectral analysis, implemented in audio analysis toolkits (e.g. librosa's spectral_spread) and MIR feature pipelines. [formal: dispersio spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
